prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1030; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported being struck while turning left at an intersection and said she felt neck and back pain shortly afterward. The claim was opened and the file assigned for review.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the collision happened as described, and the other driver's account matches the claimant's on the sequence of events. Scene photos were requested and received.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage appears largely consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that the vehicle is the insured unit on the declarations page.

Entry 5: Claimant was seen by a provider for neck and back strain. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from available records.

Entry 6: In a follow-up call, claimant described the direction of the impact differently than in the initial report. In the second conversation she also gave a different number of passengers in the car. Noted the changes and asked for clarification in writing.

Entry 7: Police and witnesses both confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, so presence at the scene is not in question. The discrepancies noted in the follow-up relate to the details of the impact and occupants.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with visits tapering as the claimant reported improvement. Medical billing reviewed and found consistent with the treatment notes.

Entry 9: File reviewed. Liability and injury appear plausible, with the open item being the clarification of the impact direction and occupant count from the claimant's changed statements before final evaluation.
